Subject: Renewal + reserved GPU increase — request for SLA exception during migration

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the renewal chat last week. As Starlight moves from a 64-GPU reserved pool to a 128-GPU committed pool to support peak inference during model retrain windows, we expect a short migration window where throughput will increase but a subset of traffic will be routed to new hardware and reprovisioned serving groups.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a temporary SLA exception for latency targets (90th/95th percentile token latency) for a 7-day cutover window during the reserved-capacity augmentation? We want to avoid automatic crediting while the team verifies kernel/quantization parity and warm caches. In exchange, Starlight agrees to the expanded committed term (12 months, committed spend + 20% burst) and an uplifted unit price for the first quarter post-cutover.

Attached: starlight_capacity_plan_v2.pdf (capacity maps, maintenance windows). Also attaching a draft redline for the commitment amendment in case procurement wants to iterate.

Proposed dates: planned cutover start — 2026-01-19 22:00 UTC, verification window — 2026-01-19 to 2026-01-26.

Next steps I recommend:
- Confirm whether Procurement needs contract language for a temporary SLA carve-out or whether an operational SLO postmortem will suffice.
- If you approve, I’ll loop in Michael from Solutions to outline fallback/rollback and warmup steps.

Ben

Thanks Olivia — putting this together now. See below for our proposed language and an operational runbook summary; full runbook attached as sla_patch_notes.txt. (See attachments in the thread.)

Proposed legal language (suggested amendment clause):
"Temporary SLA Suspension: For a period not to exceed seven (7) calendar days following the resumption of normal traffic routing after Redwood's Reserved Capacity augmentation, the latency SLOs (as defined in Section 2.1 of the Agreement) shall be considered 'under verification' and shall not automatically trigger service credit calculations provided Redwood executes the agreed verification checklist and remediation steps detailed in the attached Runbook. If latency regressions persist beyond the seven (7) day verification window and are attributable to Redwood's serving runtime or configuration changes, standard SLA credits will apply retroactively to the start of the verification window."

Operational runbook highlights (summary):
- Pre-cutover: full config snapshot; pin model versions; seed KV/prefix caches using low-priority traffic.
- Cutover: route 20% of traffic to new pool for 2 hours, increase to 50% for next 4 hours, then full shift.
- Metrics to monitor: 95th token latency, tail open-loop requests, GPU utilization, OOMs, error-rate per route.
- Rollback triggers: sustained 95th latency > baseline + 35% for 60 minutes OR error-rate spike > 1% for 30 minutes.
- Remediation: revert routing, scale-up burst pool, revert to previous quantization profile.

I’ve included Michael on technical fallbacks; Michael — can you confirm the warmup scripts and expected cache-seed timeline?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Echoing Tessa — quick technical notes from Solutions/Platform:

1) Warmup & cache seeding
- We will run overlap traffic seeding for ~12 hours pre-cutover using sampled inference requests (low priority). Full KV cache parity expected within 3 hours of 50% traffic.

2) Latency profile expectations
- Initial 95th percentile may increase by up to ~20–25% during first 6 hours while kernels stabilize and quantized kernels are validated. This is why we recommend the 7-day verification window and the staged ramp.

3) Fallback plan (fast path)
- Immediate rollback: change traffic routing at the load-balancer layer (5–10 minutes).
- If rollback not sufficient, enable temporary burst pool capacity (pre-provisioned GPUs billed per usage) for up to 72 hours.

4) Telemetry & alerts
- We’ll provide a shared Grafana dashboard and an alert subscription for the Starlight on-call rotation.

We’ll prepare a short DocuSign amendment with the suggested clause above and circulate it to Procurement and Legal once Starlight confirms acceptance.

-Michael
